configurePresets.name: base
configurePresets.description: Policy that belongs to Bump itself. Configure presets only: build, test and workflow presets multiply with every flavour and configuration, and `cmake --build <dir> --config <cfg>` and `ctest --test-dir <dir> -C <cfg>` express the same thing without a committed entry for each combination. Add your own in CMakeUserPresets.json if you want them. Everything machine-specific -- dependency locations, install prefix, target architecture, deployment target -- is deliberately absent and belongs there too. A clone with no user presets still configures if CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH is set in the environment, which CMake consults as additional search prefixes.

configurePresets.name: macos-base
configurePresets.description: Bump makes no claim about macOS architecture or deployment target. Both follow from whichever Boost you build against, so set CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES and CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in your own CMakeUserPresets.json to match it.

configurePresets.name: windows-base
configurePresets.description: Embedded debug info rather than a program database, because BUMP_WIN32_USE_MP defaults to ON and parallel compilations contend on a shared PDB. The MSVC runtime is left at CMake's default of MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>DLL, which is the dynamic CRT that bump requires anyway: it exports classes holding std::string and Boost types, so bump, Boost, googletest and every consumer must agree on it.

configurePresets.name: macos-ninja-framework
configurePresets.description: Header-set verification is off here because it only inspects FILE_SET HEADERS, and the framework flavour must use PUBLIC_HEADER instead. The static and shared presets cover that check.

configurePresets.name: macos-xcode
configurePresets.description: Scheme generation is on so every target -- including each of the eight test suites -- appears in the scheme selector and can be run or debugged on its own. Header-set verification is off because its three extra targets clutter a list the Xcode generator cannot group into folders; both Ninja presets still run it. GCC_WARN_64_TO_32_BIT_CONVERSION is off because Xcode enables it by default while Ninja does not, so with warnings as errors a Ninja-clean tree would fail under Xcode. It reports 12 real size_t-to-int narrowings, all stemming from bump's int-based length and index API; widening that API is tracked separately, and this keeps both generators checking the same things until it happens.
